verses.mystical_translation: I will extol thee, O the Living Presence; for thou hast lifted me up, and hast not made my foes to rejoice over me.
O the Living Presence my the Divine, I cried unto thee, and thou hast healed me.
the Living Presence, you brought my being up from Sheol; you kept me alive, away from those descending to the pit.
Sing unto the the Living Presence, O ye saints of his, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
For his anger endureth but a moment; in his favour is life: weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning.
And in my prosperity I said, I shall never be moved.
the Living Presence, by thy favour thou hast made my mountain to stand strong: thou didst hide thy face, and I was troubled.
I cried to thee, O the Living Presence; and unto the the Living Presence I made supplication.
What profit is there in my blood, when I go down to the pit? Shall the dust praise thee? shall it declare thy truth?
Hear, O the Living Presence, and have mercy upon me: the Living Presence, be thou my helper.
Thou hast turned for me my mourning into dancing: thou hast put off my sackcloth, and girded me with gladness;
To the end that my glory may sing praise to thee, and not be silent. O the Living Presence my the Divine, I will give thanks unto thee for ever.

contemplative_note: Night and morning become images for change: grief is real, and it is not the only possible future.
safety_note: Healing testimony is not a guarantee that every illness will resolve through faith, and suffering must not be blamed on the sufferer.
